question.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the three AIF categories under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Cat I is for hedge funds; Cat II is for start-up funds; Cat III is for private equity

Cat I invests in start-ups/early-stage/social/SME/infra/special-situation/CDMDF (sectors considered socially or economically desirable by Government); Cat II funds do not fall under Cat I or III and cannot take leverage except for temporary funding (<=30 days, <=4 times/year, <=10% investable funds) — includes PE and private debt; Cat III uses diverse/complex strategies including leverage and derivatives (hedge-fund-like)
All three categories can use unlimited leverage; the distinction is tax-based
Cat I and Cat II are open-ended; Cat III is close-ended

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 3(4)(a)-(c): Cat I — start-ups/early-stage/social/SMEs/infra/special-situation/CDMDF in socially/economically desirable sectors; Cat II — residual (PE, private credit), no leverage except temporary (<=30 days, <=4 times/year, <=10% investable funds); Cat III — diverse/complex strategies including derivatives and leverage (up to 2x NAV). Specified AIF is a fourth residual category. The Trap: Option A inverts categories. Option C is outright wrong. Option D inverts the open/close distinction. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Cat-I identification as a sales concept. XIX-B focuses on Cat III. XIX-C unifies. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: An AIF registered under a particular category cannot change category post-registration EXCEPT with SEBI approval (Regulation 8). Pick the category carefully at Form A stage based on the investment strategy and leverage plan. 'Fund of AIFs' labeling is NOT required for Cat I/II investing in other AIF units (Reg 15 clarification).
